CommandRequest.description:
One order from a bot. Which fields matter depends on CommandType CommandRequest.Type:
            * Move: units + (x,y | tile)
* Attack: units + (targetId | x,y | tile). A position means attack-move.
* Gather: units + targetId (a resource deposit)
* Build: units + buildingType + (x,y | tile)
* Produce: buildingId + unitType [+ count] [+ x,y | tile to set the rally point]
* Rally: buildingId + (x,y | tile)
* Research: buildingId + upgrade
* Stop: units
            Units are selected with string? CommandRequest.Units (e.g. "5-10", "1-7,12", "all", "idle")
            and/or int[]? CommandRequest.UnitIds, optionally narrowed by UnitType? CommandRequest.UnitType.

buildingId.description: The acting building for Produce / Research / Rally.

count.description: Produce: how many units to queue (default 1).

targetId.description: Attack target (unit or building) or Gather target (resource deposit).

tile.description: Alternative to X/Y: tile index = y * mapWidth + x.

unitIds.description: Explicit unit ids. Every id listed here must be a unit you own.

oneOf.description: For unit commands: only select units of this type. For Produce: the unit to produce.

units.description: Selector string: comma separated ids and inclusive ranges ("1-7,12"), or "all" / "idle".

commandId.description: Id of the queued command; execution outcomes are reported as events carrying this id.

bots.description: 2-16 house bot names to pit against each other, e.g. ["rusher", "economist"]. Repeat a name for several copies.

CreateLeagueMatchRequest.description:
Create a league match (admins, on the website). Verified bots join it like any match. It is played
in rounds: for each one the admin splits everyone into heats and starts them all at once.

name.description: 3-28 letters, digits, '_' or '-'. Its heats are named {name}-h1, {name}-h2, ...

tickIntervalMs.description: Milliseconds per tick in every heat.

houseBots.description: Fill seats with house bots (see GET /api/v1/bots), e.g. ["balanced"]. Repeat a name for several copies.

maxPlayers.description:
2-16 players. Default 2. Up to four start in the corners; five or more start around a ring, which
needs a bigger map (the default map size grows to fit, e.g. 120×120 for 16 players).

name.description:
Optional name so others can find the match, e.g. "cs1400-lab": 3-32 letters, digits, '_' or '-'.
No two matches that haven't finished can share a name.

EarnedAchievementDto.description: An achievement a bot has earned (GET /api/v1/players/{id}/achievements).

bots.description:
The bots that earned it, when listing a person's achievements across all their bots; empty
when listing one bot's.

matchId.description: The match that earned it, if one did.

kind.description:
Machine readable kind, e.g. CommandFailed, UnitProduced, UnitLost, UnitKilled, BuildingStarted,
BuildingCompleted, BuildingLost, BuildingDestroyed, ResearchCompleted, DepositDepleted, PlayerEliminated.

owner.description: Slot of the player the event concerns (set in spectator feeds; null for match-wide events).

GameStateDto.description: Everything one player is allowed to see this tick (fog of war applied).

buildings.description: Your buildings plus enemy buildings you can currently see.

events.description: Your recent events (command failures, completions, losses...), newest last.

paused.description: True while a spectator has paused the match. Long polls simply wait until it resumes.

rememberedBuildings.description:
Enemy buildings you have seen before that are now hidden by fog, as they were when last seen.
An entry disappears once you see its tile again and the building is gone.

resources.description: Resource deposits you can currently see.

shells.description: Siege shots in flight that you fired, or that will land on a tile you can see.

units.description: Your units plus enemy units you can currently see.

visibility.description: One string per map row (y), one char per column (x): '1' = currently visible, '0' = fogged.

HeatDto.description: One heat of a season, championship or preseason match: a separate game with some of its players.

matchId.description: The heat's own id: open it to watch, or for its result and replay.

name.description: e.g. "season-week3-h2" in the first round, "season-week3-r2-h1" in later ones.

playerIds.description: In slot order (slot 0 first), as the round seated them.

round.description: The round it belongs to; 1 for the first.

HeatStandingsDto.description: Live (or final) standings of one heat, for scoreboards.

players.description: Best first: the winner once there is one, then by score.

round.description: The round the heat belongs to; 1 for the first.

mu.description: The skill model's raw estimate: mean (starts at 25).

ownerName.description: The verified owner's name: their Discord server nickname, or Discord name. Null if unclaimed.

ownerSlug.description: The verified owner's profile name, as in #/player/{slug} and GET /api/v1/people/{slug}. Null if unclaimed.

points.description:
League points. In each match the top four (winner first, then by score) earn their score margins
over everyone below them in that four: 1st gets (s1-s2)+(s1-s3)+(s1-s4), 2nd (s2-s3)+(s2-s4),
3rd s3-s4. Season and championship ladders are ranked by points. A bot that plays two or more
heats of one league match doesn't count its lowest-scoring heat of that match.

sigma.description: The skill model's raw estimate: uncertainty (starts at 25/3 and shrinks as the bot plays).

skill.description:
Opponent-aware skill (OpenSkill, Weng-Lin Plackett-Luce): beating strong bots raises it more than
beating weak ones. Shown as max(0, round(40 x (mu - 3 sigma))), a conservative estimate, so it
starts at 0 and rises as results come in and the model grows surer. It moves in the same games as
int LeaderboardEntryDto.Rating. League ladders are ranked by points; skill is a guide, not a tiebreaker.

verified.description: True when a Discord-verified person has claimed this bot (the blue check).

MapDto.description: The static map: terrain is public knowledge, entities are not.

startPositions.description: Command Center location of each slot.

terrain.description: One string per row (y): '.' = open ground, '#' = rock (impassable).

MatchArchivePageDto.description: One page of finished matches from the archive (GET /api/v1/matches/archive), newest first.

skip.description: How many matching matches come before this page.

total.description: How many finished matches pass the filters, across every page.

MatchCategory.description: Which leaderboard a match counts toward. Each category keeps its own ratings and records.

connected.description: In a league match's queue: whether the bot made an API call in the last 40 seconds. Null elsewhere.

ownerName.description: The verified owner's name: their Discord server nickname, or Discord name. Null if unclaimed.

verified.description: True when a Discord-verified person has claimed this bot (the blue check).

MatchSpeedRequest.description: Change a running match's speed. Either field may be left out.

paused.description: Pause or resume. A paused match resumes on its own after five minutes.

tickIntervalMs.description: New milliseconds per tick, within the server's limits (100-10000 by default).

category.description: Which leaderboard the match counts toward. Matches bots create are Practice.

closed.description: A league match the admin has closed: no more rounds or players.

finalized.description: A closed league match whose points are on the ladder.

heats.description:

parentMatchId.description: For a heat: the league match it belongs to.

paused.description: True while the match is paused (see POST /api/v1/matches/{id}/speed).

speedAdjustable.description:
Whether spectators may change the speed: only matches with at most one real player (exhibitions and
games against house bots), so nobody's opponent can be sped up or paused on them.

PersonMatchDto.description: One of a person's bots in one finished match.

opponents.description: The other registered bots in the match (extra copies of a house bot aren't listed).

PersonProfileDto.description: A person's public profile: their bots, what those bots have earned, and the brawls they played.

achievements.description: Each achievement once, with the bots that earned it, newest first.

brawls.description: Their bots' most recent matches, newest first.

PlayerMatchStatsDto.description: A player's match in numbers: what they built and trained, and how they played. Used for achievements and recaps.

buildingsCompleted.description: Buildings finished, by type. The starting Command Center doesn't count.

buildingsRallied.description: Different buildings given a rally point.

commandCenterHealthPercent.description: Health of the player's healthiest Command Center when the match ended, in percent; null if they had none.

commandsFailed.description: Commands that failed when they ran (CommandFailed events).

depositsExhausted.description: Resource deposits this player's workers mined dry.

enemyCommandCenterSeenTick.description: Tick this player first saw an enemy Command Center, if they did.

firstBarracksTick.description: Tick the first Barracks was finished, if one was.

firstCombatUnitTick.description: Tick the first Soldier, Archer or Scout was ready, if one was.

guardTowersStanding.description: Completed guard towers standing when the match ended.

longestWorkerIdleTicks.description: Longest stretch, in ticks, any one worker spent idle.

lowestScoreSharePercent.description:
The lowest this player's score fell relative to the leader's, in percent (100 = never behind),
checked every 10 ticks from tick 100 while they were still in the match.

oreWasted.description: Ore workers brought home that didn't fit in storage.

serumKills.description: Enemy units killed by serum-boosted soldiers.

serumTaken.description: Whether this player took the serum.

towerKills.description: Enemy units killed by this player's guard towers.

unitsTrained.description: Units trained, by type. The starting workers don't count.

ownerName.description: The verified owner's name: their Discord server nickname, or Discord name. Null if unclaimed.

ownerSlug.description: The verified owner's profile name, as in #/player/{slug} and GET /api/v1/people/{slug}. Null if unclaimed.

rating.description: Practice rating. Season and championship ratings are in IReadOnlyList<CategoryRecordDto> PlayerProfileDto.Records.

records.description: Rating and record in each category (Practice, Season, Championship).

skill.description: Practice skill (see int LeaderboardEntryDto.Skill). Other categories' are in IReadOnlyList<CategoryRecordDto> PlayerProfileDto.Records.

verified.description: True when a Discord-verified person has claimed this bot (the blue check).

wins.description: Practice record. Season and championship records are in IReadOnlyList<CategoryRecordDto> PlayerProfileDto.Records.

oneOf.description: How the match went for this player, in more detail. Null for matches recorded before these were kept.

PublishRecapRequest.description: What the recap job publishes once it has uploaded the video (POST /api/v1/recaps).

video.description: The video's blob name in the recaps container, or an absolute URL.

earnedBy.description: How many bots have it now.

mentoring.description: The mentoring reminder to work in.

news.description: Game changes that shipped this day: the hosts announce them near the top of the show.

quiet.description: Few matches: make a short episode.

recentEpisodes.description: Recent episodes' titles, newest first, so the show doesn't repeat itself.

rulesNotes.description: Rules facts for a "tip of the night".

RecapEpisodeDto.description: A published episode, as the website lists it.

transcript.description: The script; only when one episode is asked for.

videoUrl.description: Where to play it (redirects to the video).

rankedBy.description: "rating" for practice, "points" for the league ladders.

previousRank.description: Rank the night before; null if they weren't on it.

RecapLineDto.description: One line of an episode's script.

RecapLoreDto.description: What things are called on this server.

names.description: Extra flavor the hosts may use (house bot nicknames, building and upgrade names).

ore.description: "ore", or "grubs" in the Snow College theme.

why.description: Why it was picked, e.g. "comeback from 31% of the leader's score".

details.description: What changed and how bots use it, API names included.

facts.description: A few short facts for the big screen.

RecapNoteDto.description: Something worth a line on the show, with the match it happened in.

newForBot.description: The bot hadn't played this way before (it had played before).

newOnServer.description: Nobody had played this way before.

usedToPlay.description: How the bot usually played before, if that was different.

realMatches.description: Matches with at least two real (non-house) bots from different people.

leagueMatches.description: League matches created and taking players now.

nextLeagueDay.description: The next league day, if the days are configured, e.g. "Tuesday, October 27".

schedule.description: When league matches are played, in words.

apiKey.description: Send as "Authorization: Bearer {apiKey}". Shown only once — store it.

ReplayDto.description: Everything needed to deterministically re-simulate a match.

commands.description: Commands in the order they were queued, each with the tick it was queued on.

mapWidth.description: Map size and seed: the map is generated from these, so it isn't stored.

oneOf.description: How the match ended; null while it is still being played.

ReplayFramesDto.description:
How to play back a finished match frame by frame: what spectators saw on every tick, in chunks of
int ReplayFramesDto.ChunkTicks ticks. Fetch chunk `n` from `/frames/{n}`: newline-separated
SpectatorStateDtos for ticks `n * ChunkTicks` onward, one per line.

lastTick.description: The last tick with a frame: where the match ended.

rebuilt.description:
The match was played before frames were recorded, so they were rebuilt from its replay
(and checked against the recorded result).

rulesVersion.description:
The game rules the match was played under. Frames show what happened then, whatever the rules
are now.

RulesDto.description: Static game data so bots can be data driven instead of hard-coding numbers.

destruction.description: Resource value of enemy units and buildings destroyed.

survival.description: Resource value of your surviving units and completed buildings.

incomePerMinute.description: Ore banked over the last 60 ticks (one minute at normal speed).

ShellDto.description:
A siege shot in flight. It lands on tile (x, y) at the end of int ShellDto.LandsTick and hits every
enemy of its owner standing there then; anything that has moved off the tile is missed.

attackerId.description: The unit that fired it (it may have died since).

incomePerMinute.description: Ore banked over the last 60 ticks (one minute at normal speed).

visibility.description: Visibility rows for this player (same format as GameStateDto.Visibility).

SpectatorStateDto.description: Omniscient view for spectators: every entity, every player's economy.

SplitHeatsRequest.description: How many players go in each heat of the next round; the sizes must add up to everyone who joined.

place.description: 1 = best; equal scores share a place.

points.description: League points for this heat: final once it has ended, otherwise what they'd get if it ended now.

TelemetryLinkDto.description: A link from the admin section of the account page to an Azure portal page.

TrophyRoomEntryDto.description: One row of the Trophy Room: a person and what their bots have earned between them.

achievements.description: Different achievements earned by any of their bots (each counts once).

points.description: Trophy points: 1 per Bronze, 2 per Silver, 4 per Gold, 8 per Platinum. The Trophy Room is ranked by these.

targetId.description: Current target entity (attack target, deposit, construction site), if any.

minRange.description: Targets closer than this (Chebyshev) are too close to hit. 0 = no minimum.

range.description: Attack reach in tiles (Chebyshev distance: diagonals count as 1).

shotTicks.description:
0 = attacks land at once. Otherwise the unit lobs a shell at the target's tile that lands this many
ticks later, hitting every enemy on that tile then; targets that move off it are missed.

speed.description: Tenths of a tile per tick (10 = one tile per tick).

info.description: Bots play Badger Brawl, Snow College's bot-programming RTS, over this API. Unit and building names here are the classic ones (ore is grubs on the field, and a CommandCenter is your campus HQ, like the Noyes Building). Register with POST /api/v1/players to get an API key, then send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The full rules are in GET /api/v1/rules.
